articles.excerpt_original: Electronic correlations in graphene are generally considered weak due to the large bandwidth of its π electrons. Here we show that tensile expansion of the honeycomb lattice provides a direct route to enhancing correlation effects. Using variational and diffusion quantum Monte Carlo, we compare a conventional Jastrow-Slater determinant wave function with a resonating-valence-bond (RVB) Jastrow-antisymmetrized geminal product ansatz for a series of stretched graphene lattices. We find that the energy gain of the RVB state relative to the single-determinant description increases with bond expansion up to a critical strain δ cr , and decreases beyond it, revealing a nonmonotonic evolution of electronic correlations. A quantitative analysis places δ cr ≈ 14 –19% across the system sizes studied, extrapolating to 13.7 ± 0.8 % in the thermodynamic limit. Analysis of the optimized many-body pairing amplitude further reveals that this crossover is accompanied by a sharp, specific enhancement of π -orbital character in the nearest-neighbor pairing between adjacent carbon atoms, providing direct microscopic evidence for the emergence of RVB-like bonding. This behavior indicates a transition from a weakly correlated Dirac semimetal to a regime with enhanced nondynamic correlation and short-range singlet pairing. Our results provide direct many-body evidence that lattice expansion drives graphene into a regime where RVB-like correlations become energetically favorable, offering a simple route to tuning correlation effects in Dirac materials.

articles.excerpt_original: Graphene holds significant potential for terahertz (THz) dynamic modulators due to its ultrafast electrical tunability. However, existing graphene metasurface modulators struggle to simultaneously achieve high modulation depth, wide optical operating bandwidth, and ultrafast electrical switching speed. In this paper, we propose a novel, to our knowledge, electrically controlled transmissive THz modulator based on a graphene-Huygens metasurface. Integrating monolayer graphene into the strong-field coupling gaps of miniaturized Huygens unit cells allows for dynamic tuning of the Fermi level via a gate voltage, thereby manipulating electromagnetic resonances. Leveraging the Huygens electromagnetic dipole matching principle and a multi-subunit mode overlap mechanism, this device effectively mitigates the inherent trade-offs among these performance metrics. Simulation results demonstrate that the device achieves a modulation depth of 10.4 dB and an operating bandwidth of 335 GHz (a fractional bandwidth of 62%) while maintaining an insertion loss of 2.21 dB. Furthermore, through a low-parasitic unit cell design and optimized low-resistance gate routing, the device is predicted to achieve a −3-dB modulation bandwidth of up to 1.056 GHz, showing strong potential to meet the requirements of high-resolution imaging and on-chip communication systems. This study provides a promising design paradigm for the development of high-speed, high-efficiency, and broadband THz dynamic devices.

bulletin.title: Graphene Weekly Bulletin — Week ending 2026-08-30
bulletin.introduction: This week’s evidence points to continued broadening of graphene’s application pipeline, led by thermal management, composites and sensing. Research advances emphasize performance through material architecture, dispersion, doping and process control, while new deposition and metrology work addresses integration and reproducibility. Commercial activity is emerging in cooling, defense supply and production scale-up, but disclosed validation and deployment details remain limited. The near-term pattern is therefore one of technical maturation alongside selective, still early-stage commercialization.

company_updates.blurb: Graphene Manufacturing Group has launched G FLUID, a graphene-based coolant additive for data-center cooling systems, marking a concrete commercialization step in thermal management. The supplied source, however, provides no independent evidence on performance or customer adoption.

Renhai Technology has applied for a patent on a graphene–copper foam composite heat sink, specifying an overall density of 0.7–3.8 g/cm³. The application claims lightweight thermal performance and improved stability, corrosion and oxidation resistance, but these claims remain unverified.

academic.blurb: A single-piece potentiometric sensor incorporates graphene directly within a Pb(II)-selective membrane, removing a separate solid-contact layer. The optimized device reported a 6.3 × 10−8 M detection limit, a 1.0 × 10−7–1.0 × 10−2 M linear range, and low potential drift.

academic.blurb: Adding 0.5 wt% graphene allowed fluorosilicone rubber to retain more than 90% of tensile strength after 72 hours at 230°C. Electron paramagnetic resonance attributed the improved thermal-oxidative stability to radical scavenging and suppression of oxidation-related chain scission.

academic.blurb: A room-temperature graphene detector was monolithically integrated on a high-resistivity silicon dielectric waveguide for D-band operation. It achieved 11.5 V/W responsivity and 1.94 GHz bandwidth, supporting the prospect of integrated terahertz photonic circuits for communications, spectroscopy and sensing.

A continuous graphene-fiber thermocouple uses periodic PEI and FeCl₃ doping to form in-fiber p–n pairs. It delivered 452.32 µV K−1 sensitivity, retained about 97.8% performance after 10,000 bends, and measured skin temperature with 0.64% error.

PET/graphene nanocomposites using a three-dimensional graphene nanoplatelet network were examined as gas barriers. At 0.3 wt% graphene, surface-area and pore-volume changes supported enhanced barrier performance, although results depended on dispersion, loading, aspect ratio and interfacial interactions.

academic.blurb: A characterization-led method fractionates commercial graphene oxide to select precursors for more uniform electrostatic deposition on cotton. Raman, DLS, zeta-potential and XPS measurements link sheet dimensions and chemical functionalization to coating performance, enabling process monitoring and batch comparison.

This review assesses metal–graphene and graphene oxide catalysts for advanced oxidation processes, pollutant removal, water splitting and CO2 photoreduction. It identifies reduced metal-ion agglomeration and enhanced adsorption as potential support benefits, while highlighting pilot- and real-scale remediation as future needs.
